children: By Megan Cheah and Kimberley Kao
The National Stock Exchange of India is seeking a valuation of $46 billion in a long-awaited initial public offering that would make it one of the country's most valuable companies.

The operator of India's largest stock exchange set a price band of 1,700 rupees to 1,785 rupees a share for the sale of 126.4 million existing shares, with no new capital being raised, it said Friday.
The number of shares being offered was reduced by around 15% from the estimate in the draft prospectus filed in June.
At the top of the price range, the IPO would value the company at 4.418 trillion rupees, equivalent to $46.17 billion, based on its total shares outstanding.
The offer opens next Thursday and closes Sept. 21.
Selling shareholders include State Bank of India, the Canada Pension Plan Investment Board and Morgan Stanley.
The exchange first filed to go public in 2016 but faced years of delays because of regulatory disputes and legal proceedings.
Its smaller rival BSE, formerly known as the Bombay Stock Exchange, listed in 2017.
NSE is India's largest stock exchange by turnover in cash and equity-derivatives markets.
It had more than 3,000 listed companies with a combined market capitalization of nearly $5 trillion as of June 30, according to the exchange's prospectus.
Net profit for the fiscal year ended in March was more than $1 billion, down 15% from a year earlier.

NSE's $2.36 billion IPO would be among India's largest listings this year, likely rivalling that of Reliance Industries' Jio Platforms, which filed its draft IPO prospectus in June. The offering would still fall short of Hyundai Motor India's $3.32 billion IPO in 2024.
The highly anticipated offering comes amid macroeconomic uncertainty that has weighed on Indian stocks.

Listing activity has remained relatively subdued this year, while the benchmark Sensex index has fallen more than 12% as investors contend with weaker risk appetite, concerns about valuations and the effects of the Middle East conflict.
